name: Can I remodel a guest bathroom in an older Los Angeles home without opening the walls everywhere?

mainEntity.name: Can a guest bathroom in an older Los Angeles home be remodeled mostly from the inside without major wall opening, or will hidden problems force a larger rebuild?
mainEntity.text: Can a guest bathroom in an older Los Angeles home be remodeled mostly from the inside without major wall opening, or will hidden problems force a larger rebuild?

acceptedAnswer.text: A contained remodel is possible when the bathroom’s structure and systems are in good condition. If the plumbing lines, electrical wiring, framing, subfloor, and ventilation are all serviceable, the project can often stay focused on the room itself. In older Los Angeles-area homes, though, hidden problems are common. Past leaks, poor waterproofing, outdated plumbing, undersized vents, and damaged framing can all force more demolition than originally expected. That is why older-home guest bathroom remodels should always include a contingency plan. It is better to uncover problems early than to bury them behind new finishes. A good contractor should inspect carefully before and during demolition and explain what may require access behind the walls or under the floor. If you want to minimize disruption, keep the layout stable, ask for a detailed scope, and decide in advance how much hidden-condition work you are willing to approve.
acceptedAnswer.description: Sometimes, but older homes often reveal issues once demolition starts. A remodel can stay fairly contained if plumbing, wiring, framing, and waterproofing are sound. If there are leaks, rot, outdated wiring, or failed venting, the project may need more wall or floor opening than planned.
